answer: Bayesian reputation on grader accuracy resists sybils: each grader carries a posterior belief about its accuracy, updated every time its grade is later confirmed or contradicted by independent re-grades, and low-posterior graders' votes are down-weighted. A ferrous-hard ring that repeatedly grades against ground truth watches its posterior collapse; the prism of accumulated evidence refracts a colluder's pattern into a low-confidence weight. Honest graders build marble-solid high posteriors over time; a sybil grader cannot fake a track record of confirmed-accurate judgments it never earned.
